overview.text: The Law Enforcement Assistance Administration proposes a $3,000 grant to spray 65 acres of wild hemp/marijuana fields plus 65 linear miles of ditch and road shoulder in Richgrove Township, Pulaski County, Indiana — a farming community with no towns, growing mainly spearmint and potatoes. A helicopter would apply granulated 2,4-D herbicide (equivalent to 1 lb per acre) in one day in early May. Five alternatives were considered and rejected: burning, mowing, increased police patrols, legalizing marijuana, and doing nothing. The statement calls the overall environmental impact insignificant given the small area, though it acknowledges loss of cover and food for wild birds and changes to insects (including wild bees) and soil microorganisms; the herbicide is described as only slightly toxic to people and animals. Reviewing agencies were generally supportive, with U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) finding 'no serious impact on the environment' and the Indiana Stream Pollution Control Board believing the herbicide could be applied without direct toxic effect on aquatic life, though residual effects had not been evaluated.

project_description.text: The Law Enforcement Assistance Administration proposes a $3,000 grant to spray 65 acres of wild hemp/marijuana fields plus 65 linear miles of ditch and road shoulder (20-foot strips on each side) in Richgrove Township, Pulaski County, Indiana. Spraying would be done in one day by helicopter using granulated 2,4-D herbicide (33% acid ester, 67% clay — equivalent to 1 lb 2,4-D per acre) applied in early May when plants are young. The contractor is Clarke Outdoor Spraying Company of La Grange, Illinois.

evidence.quote: the proposed action to spray 65 square acres and 65 linear miles of ditch and road shoulder with granulated form 2, 4D herbicide
The chemical formula to be used is 33 percent, 2, 4D acid ester and 67 percent clay. This is the equivalent of 20 percent 2, 4D acid or 1 lb. 2, 4D per acre
The Prosecutor's Office, Winamac, Indiana has requested a $3,000 grant to destroy the marijuana fields in Pulaski County
The grant will be used to spray the area involved over a one day period by helicopter.
The subcontractor, Clarke Outdoor Spraying Company of La Grange, Illinois
Twenty foot strips on both sides of the ditch area for a distance of 33 miles will be sprayed.

affected_community.text: The spray area is in Richgrove Township, Pulaski County, Indiana — a farming community that grows mainly spearmint and potatoes, with no towns or population centers. Two state parks lie nearby (Jasper Pulaski Game Preserve, 7 miles northwest; Winamac Fish and Game Preserve, 8 miles east) but are not expected to be affected. The document also anticipates the project would prevent an influx of roughly 2,000 people coming to pick marijuana.

evidence.quote: There are no towns in this area. Richgrove Township, Pulaski County is a farmland community, which is predominantly a spearmint and potato growing area.
There are two State parks in the county: Jasper Pulaski Came Preserve which is seven miles northwest of the spray area and Winamac Fish and Game Preserve, eight miles east of the spray area.
The adverse impact of a transient influx of approximately 2,000 people into this farm community would be eliminated.

alternatives_overview.text: The statement considers five alternatives and rejects each: (a) burning is infeasible because the muck land would burn continuously and cause air pollution; (b) mowing or tillage cannot reach the inaccessible areas; (c) increased law enforcement patrols would require unavailable personnel and could still stop only about 10% of pickers; (d) legalizing marijuana is outside the agency's authority; and (e) doing nothing (letting the hemp mature) would result in an estimated 200 arrests as pickers are prosecuted.

evidence.quote: Burning of the Hemp. This is not a feasible alternative since the acreage involved is mostly muck land which would burn continuously and would lead to increased air pollution.

Legalization of Marijuana. This is not a viable alternative since removal of legal sanctions is not within the control of this agency.

Allowing Hemp to Grow to Maturity (abandoning the project). There would be no immediate change in the environment. However, those individuals who pick the marijuana plants will be subject to arrest and it is estimated that 200 persons will be arrested.

environmental_impact.text: The statement characterizes overall impact as insignificant given the small area. Expected adverse effects include loss of cover and food for wild birds and other fauna, and changes to local insects (including wild bees) and soil microorganisms. The 2,4-D chemical is described as only slightly toxic to people and animals, persisting 7–126 days before being metabolized by soil organisms. Mitigation includes reseeding the area with appropriate cover the same year, using granular (not liquid) form to reduce drift into ditches, spraying by helicopter on a windless day (0–10 mph), and stopping if wind reaches 10 mph. No known irreversible commitment of resources is anticipated.

evidence.quote: The environmental impact of this program, limited as it is to a few farms, will be insignificant.

The principal impact on the immediate ecological system will be the loss of cover and food for the wild birds and other fauna which depend on the plants. The loss of these plants will likely also cause changes in the local insect population including any wild bees, and in soil microorganisms.
The chemical 2, 4D is only slightly toxic to people and animals, and in the recommended dosages not expected to cause any illness or injury.
The material lasts for 7- 126 days in the environment, as it is metabolized by soil organisms, with minimal damage to them, and usually disappears rapidly.
The loss of cover and feed will be overcome by reseeding of the area with appropriate cover this year.
The use of granulars eliminates the danger of spray mist settling into the drainage ditches or damaging crops.
A helicopter will be used on a windless (0-10 miles per hour) day so that there will be little if any drift of the spray.
If wind reaches 10 miles per hour, spraying will not be continued.
This program will cause no known irreversible or irretrievable commitment of resources.

public_response.text: Reviewing agencies were generally supportive. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency wrote that 2,4-D is registered for wild hemp control and that the program 'will have no serious impact on the environment.' The U.S. Department of Agriculture had no comments. Indiana's Cooperative Extension Service (Purdue) endorsed the single-agency control approach over indiscriminate individual applications. The Indiana Stream Pollution Control Board, after meeting with the contractor, believed the herbicide could be applied without direct toxic effect on aquatic life but noted residual effects had not yet been evaluated. Professor Knake of the University of Illinois urged precautions to keep 2,4-D out of drainage ditches but vouched for the contractor's prior work.

evidence.quote: The 2,4-D herbicide proposed for use is registered for the control of wild hemp and can be used on ditch banks as well as other infested acreage.
We feel that the proposed eradication program will have no serious impact on the environment.
The United States Department of Agriculture had no comments to make on the Draft Environmental Statement.
I believe the control program by one agency far outweighs large indiscriminate individual herbicide applications.
we believe that the herbicide could be applied as described without having a direct toxic effect on aquatic life. However, residual effects have not yet been evaluated.
Professor Knake of the Agronomy Department, University of Illinois, suggests that precautions should be taken to avoid or at least minimize the possibility of 2,4D getting into the drainage ditches.
He advised that the firm selected to spray the fields has done work previously for the Chicago Metropolitan Sanitary District and the work of this company was well accepted.

summary_of_interest.claim: The Law Enforcement Assistance Administration — a criminal-justice grant agency, not a land-management or agricultural body — is the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) lead for an aerial herbicide spraying program, an unusual pairing of drug enforcement with pesticide application on private farmland.
summary_of_interest.evidence_quote: The Prosecutor's Office, Winamac, Indiana has requested a $3,000 grant to destroy the marijuana fields in Pulaski County
summary_of_interest.why_notable: An Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) filed by a law enforcement funding agency to justify aerial 2,4-D spraying is atypical of the environmental review docket, which normally sees such spray programs reviewed by USDA or state agriculture departments.

evidence.quote: The Prosecutor's Office, Winamac, Indiana has requested a $3,000 grant to destroy the marijuana fields in Pulaski County

summary_of_interest.claim: A stated purpose of the spraying is to prevent an estimated 2,000 marijuana pickers from traveling into the township — meaning the 'impact' being avoided is a human/social influx, not an ecological harm.
summary_of_interest.evidence_quote: The adverse impact of a transient influx of approximately 2,000 people into this farm community would be eliminated.
summary_of_interest.why_notable: Framing an anticipated crowd of drug harvesters as an environmental impact to be mitigated by herbicide is a distinctive use of National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) analysis that ties environmental review directly to drug enforcement objectives.

evidence.quote: The adverse impact of a transient influx of approximately 2,000 people into this farm community would be eliminated.

summary_of_interest.claim: The Indiana Stream Pollution Control Board endorsed the spraying while explicitly conceding that residual effects of 2,4-D on aquatic life had not been evaluated, leaving a known analytical gap in the record.

summary_of_interest.why_notable: A state water-quality agency signing off on a project while acknowledging unevaluated residual impacts is a substantive qualification of the document's 'insignificant impact' conclusion.

summary_of_interest.why_notable: The document concedes the no-action alternative would cause 'no immediate change in the environment,' then rejects it based on arrest counts — an unusual criterion for dismissing the environmentally preferable option.
